summary: This resolution sets House floor procedures for debating and voting on H.R. 556 (barring federal lead-ammunition bans), H.R. 1958 (making immigration fraud or benefit misuse grounds for inadmissibility), and H.R. 4638 (same for harming police animals), by waiving points of order, adopting committee substitutes, limiting each to one hour of debate plus one recommit motion, and extending debate on a balanced-budget suspension motion.

scores.thoughts: The resolution facilitates consideration of H.R. 1958, which targets unlawful receipt of public benefits by making such convictions grounds for inadmissibility/deportation. This has a tangential effect on government spending by aiming to reduce improper expenditures on benefits, but the primary focus is immigration enforcement rather than direct spending cuts.

The resolution makes H.R. 556 in order, which prohibits federal agencies from banning lead ammunition on public lands. This directly protects gun/hunting rights by removing regulatory restrictions on ammunition choice.

Two of the three bills advanced (H.R. 1958 and H.R. 4638) amend the Immigration and Nationality Act to expand grounds for inadmissibility and deportability based on specific criminal convictions. This strongly advances immigration enforcement and border/security priorities.

H.R. 556, advanced by this resolution, blocks federal prohibitions on lead ammunition and tackle. Lead is an environmental toxin, so preventing restrictions on its use limits environmental protections on federal lands.

H.R. 1958 penalizes unlawful receipt of public benefits via immigration consequences. This indirectly supports scaling back improper use of welfare programs by strengthening enforcement against fraud.
